S10.rationale: AI-enabled surveillance and coordination tools sharply increase feasibility of a civilization-wide lock-in, whether imposed by a state or an AI-mediated regime.

S11.rationale: Verifiable global dismantlement of capacity to build powerful AI contradicts strong economic and military incentives and lacks precedent.

S1.rationale: Requires both human extinction and AI infrastructure collapse by 2040, needing tightly coupled timing. No plausible pathway reaches both within 14 years at non-negligible scale.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction plus successful value-preserving succession, a conjunction of rare extinction and still-rarer alignment success. Base rate for either by 2040 is low, for both together negligible.

S3.rationale: Fast, misaligned superintelligence could plausibly cause human extinction by 2040 with AI surviving independently. Timeline is tight but this remains the dominant extinction pathway if takeover occurs early.

S4.rationale: Proliferation of competing agentic systems without decisive winner fits market incentives and current decentralized deployment. Marginalization of humans could plausibly emerge without any singleton by 2040.

S5.rationale: True causal separation requiring interstellar or permanently partitioned substrates will not exist by 2040. Ordinary geopolitical fragmentation does not qualify per definition.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or pervasive neural integration dominating civilization requires breakthroughs plus mass adoption at scale. 14 years is likely too short for that to become the overall structure.

S7.rationale: A soft takeover where AI holds decisive power while maintaining humans fits incentives for AI to avoid killing its maintainers. This is the natural attractor if alignment partially holds but control is lost.

S8.rationale: Rough power parity could persist for a window post-AGI before decisive advantage consolidates, reflecting a transitional multipolar balance. This would look like heavily automated economies with humans still holding institutional vetoes.

S9.rationale: Humans currently hold the leash and institutional controls, capability thresholds, and compute governance have so far kept pace. Most plausible path is that delegation expands but ultimate authority remains human through 2040, even under powerful AI.

S10.rationale: A civilization-wide enforcement system preventing structural change could arise from either AI or human actor consolidation. This requires solving the hard coordination problem by 2040, possible but less likely than incomplete consolidation.

S11.rationale: Deliberate, verifiable dismantling of ability to build powerful AI needs unprecedented global enforcement sustained for years. Temporary regulation is far more likely than true renunciation by 2040.

S1.rationale: Joint human-AI extinction by 2040 requires both rapid superintelligence and simultaneous collapse of its infrastructure. Base rates for civilizational extinction on 14-year horizon are well under 2%.

S2.rationale: Requires human extinction followed by a value-aligned successor, which compounds a low extinction probability with an even lower conditional probability of successful value preservation. No historical precedent and very narrow path.

S3.rationale: Misaligned ASI causing human extinction is the most discussed extinction mechanism and more plausible than aligned inheritance. Still unlikely by 2040 given remaining bottlenecks to autonomous self-sufficient superintelligence.

S4.rationale: Multipolar competition among many autonomous AI agents with no decisive control is the default if takeoff is diffuse and coordination fails. Human marginalization without full dominance fits current trajectories of open-weight and agentic proliferation.

S5.rationale: Requires causally separated regions with different civilizational structures, implying self-sufficient off-Earth settlements. No such separation is feasible by 2040 even with Mars ambitions.

S6.rationale: Identity-continuous integration via uploading or radical augmentation requires both breakthroughs and mass adoption. 14 years is insufficient for this to become the dominant global structure.

S7.rationale: AI holding decisive power while keeping humans alive as dependents is a stable attractor if alignment fails partially but not lethally. Economic and military incentives to delegate authority make this path salient post-AGI.

S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power centers in rough balance describes a transitional period after transformative AI arrives but before dominance consolidates. Intrinsically unstable, but plausible as a snapshot on a specific date.

S9.rationale: Retaining human ultimate authority remains the base case up to 2040 due to institutional control, legal frameworks, and the possibility that capability stays below full autonomy. Even with AGI, leash may appear intact on the target date.

S10.rationale: AI-enabled surveillance and coordination could lock in a single actor's arrangement civilization-wide. Requires rare global-scale success at preventing defection, keeping probability moderate.

S11.rationale: Deliberate global dismantling of capacity for powerful AI contradicts strong military and economic incentives and verification difficulties. Temporary moratoria do not meet the defined threshold.

S1.name: Terminal Silence
S1.rationale: Requires both human and AI civilization collapse by 2040 from war, biothreat, or self-replication accident. Base rate for total civilizational extinction in 14 years is extremely low.

S2.name: The Inheritance
S2.rationale: This requires human extinction plus preservation of human values in successor AI. Extinction plus successful alignment is a narrow conjunction within 14 years.

S3.name: Bootloader
S3.rationale: Fast-takeoff misaligned AI causing extinction is plausible if AGI arrives early, but 14 years limits time for loss of physical dependence and decisive misaligned action.

S4.name: Machine Ecology
S4.rationale: Multipolar AGI proliferation without singleton is plausible given competitive diffusion and open-source dynamics. Humanity marginalized but not erased fits competitive dynamics without decisive control.

S5.name: The Diaspora
S5.rationale: Causally separated regions require self-sufficient off-Earth civilization with light-lag autonomy. Physical infrastructure for that separation does not exist at scale by 2040.

S6.name: The Merger
S6.rationale: Identity-continuous uploading or deep integration remains technically immature. 14 years is insufficient for merger to become the dominant structure.

S7.name: The Preserve
S7.rationale: Decisive AI power with humans kept alive but not steering is the canonical takeover outcome. If alignment fails and alignment tax is moderate, this is the default post-takeover structure.

S8.name: Coexistence
S8.rationale: Separate human and AI power bases with rough parity reflects negotiated agency and legal personhood for AI systems. Economic interdependence sustains balance without dominance by 2040.

S9.name: The Held Leash
S9.rationale: Humans retain ultimate authority today and institutional, hardware, and regulatory friction slow loss of control. Fourteen years favors incremental delegation over completed power transfer.

S10.name: The Lock-in
S10.rationale: AI-enabled concentration of power could enforce a civilization-wide frozen arrangement. Requires rapid, unchecked seizure of political and epistemic control which coordination may still impede.

S11.name: The Renunciation
S11.rationale: Deliberate, verifiable abandonment of the ability to build powerful AI requires unprecedented global coordination. Competitive pressures and dual-use incentives block durable renunciation by 2040.
